title: Document the external-trigger contract for a cold supervisor tick
action: PBI sup-20260831-7f3a (bee-side half of making bee supervisor actually run) named four gaps. Investigation found gaps 1 and 2 already shipped (mailbox delivery at the UserPromptSubmit turn boundary, and --role dispatch|merge|supervisor parsing) with no code change needed. Gap 3 (a documented contract for a tick triggered from outside, waggledance being the caller) and gap 4 (the notebook's causal shape) both resolve without new code: gap 3 by documenting the existing `--role supervisor --once --main-root PATH` subprocess-spawn primitive, gap 4 by deferring a heavier notebook shape to a parked PBI rather than adding validation that would fight the locked terse-note decision (c80debd7). Add an 'External trigger (cross-repo callers)' section to docs/knowledge/areas/bee-herding/the-supervisor-observer-and-its-interventions.md documenting the contract, its exit-code semantics, and its concurrency safety.

truths: The knowledge-area doc names the exact --once --main-root invocation as the external-trigger primitive.
The doc states the invocation needs no tmux/herdr pane, citing the subprocess spawn path.
The doc states the exit-code contract (0 on completed/timed-out, 1 only on spawn failure).
The doc states repeated/concurrent invocation is safe because stores are append-only and the point-key frequency cap absorbs duplicates.
bee knowledge check reports zero OKF/profile errors after the edit.

acceptance: The knowledge-area doc documents the external-trigger contract in full (primitive, transport, exit codes, concurrency safety, no verb-surface change), and bee knowledge check is green.

trace.outcome: Documented the --once --main-root external-trigger contract in the bee-herding supervisor knowledge area

report.outcome: Added an External trigger (cross-repo callers) section documenting the --role supervisor --once --main-root PATH primitive: no pane needed, exit-code contract, and concurrency safety via append-only stores + the point-key frequency cap.
